newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp sees no inflation danger at present.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp sees no inflation danger at present.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Thursday that he saw no inflationary dangers for the German economy at the moment.

Asked whether the recent depreciation of the mark had been weathered without increasing inflationary risks in Germany, Krupp said "that depends on how the economy develops. It is hard to assess. The information we have so far shows no need for concern on the price front."
Krupp is also the president of the state central bank in Hamburg.
Buba's Krupp sees no inflation danger at =2
Earlier on Thursday, the federal statistics office in Wiesbaden said that April inflation measured 1.4 percent compared with year ago levels.
This is far below the Bundesbank's traditional two percent inflation goal.
When asked to comment about currencies, Krupp said the mark was "in a normalisation phase, not in a depreciation phase".
He declined to comment on the current level of the dollar. "It is not the task of any commentator to do fine-tuning," he said.
Asked whether he expected the G7 to issue another statement on the dollar at its meeting in Washington this weekend, Krupp said: "I don't know what the G7 will do, I won't be there."
In February, G7 ministers meeting in Berlin said the dollar's rise had gone far enough.
